**Finding: compliant** — no redline proposed.

Section 15.2 (Assignment; Change of Control) lands at or above our preferred position:

- **Our assignment rights:** we may assign to any Sanofi Affiliate without RevMed's consent (p0610), and without consent to a successor in a merger, acquisition or similar transaction, or a sale of all or substantially all related assets (p0611) — the affiliate/M&A carve-out the playbook requires.
- **RevMed's assignment rights are constrained:** affiliate assignments require our consent (not to be unreasonably withheld, delayed or conditioned), and RevMed cannot transfer the RevMed Licensed Patents to a Third Party without our consent (p0615).
- **Competitor protection:** RevMed's consent-free Change of Control assignment is conditioned on the Acquiror Family firewall in p0613–p0614 (wholly-owned subsidiary, IP/R&D assets retained, separation from Acquiror competing programs, no Know-How exchange). RevMed's reciprocal successor right sits at the fallback ("mutual right to assign to successors") and is offset by our termination/alternative option on a RevMed Change of Control (Section 12.2(a)(ii), p0489).
- **No walk-away trigger:** RevMed has no termination or re-pricing right on a Sanofi change of control; its termination rights run only to material breach, insolvency, competing product and cessation.

Noted in the rationale but not flagged as deviations: the Section 9.7(a) withholding gross-up where tax arises from our assignment to an Affiliate, and the cessation of post-termination royalties payable to us upon a Change of Control of Sanofi (p0508) — narrow economic points, not vendor exit rights.
